```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4)
library(spCVAudit)
```

A selection rule compares candidate CV schemes for the **same target and final
prediction model**. It seeks a useful estimate of that model's target MSE. It
does not seek the smallest CV score.

## Specify candidates and a weighted target

```{r design}
set.seed(101)
training <- matrix(runif(120), ncol = 2)
q <- as.matrix(expand.grid(x = seq(0.1, 1.3, length.out = 8),
                          y = seq(0.1, 0.9, length.out = 8)))
target <- prediction_target(q, weights = ifelse(q[, 1] > 1, 2, 1),
                            label = "Target with extra weight beyond the sampled region")
schemes <- list(
  random = spatial_folds(training, 5, "random", seed = 4),
  block = spatial_folds(training, 5, "block", seed = 4),
  buffered = spatial_folds(training, 5, "buffered", buffer = 0.04, seed = 4)
)
model <- spatial_covariance(range = 0.2, signal = 0.8)
```

The buffer removes training observations within 0.04 coordinate units of a test
observation. If this empties a training set, the constructor reports an error;
reduce the buffer or reconsider the partition. Matching seeds gives block and
buffered schemes the same test groups.

## Compare two selection criteria

```{r compare}
by_W <- compare_cv_schemes(training, schemes, target, model, criterion = "W")
by_J2 <- compare_cv_schemes(training, schemes, target, model, criterion = "J2")
by_W
by_J2
```

`W` measures a distance-distribution discrepancy. `abs(J2)` compares average
squared correlation and can allow cancellation. They need not select the same
scheme. A single common covariance specification is used for all candidates.

If covariance is estimated from observed training responses, pass an
`estimate_covariance(training, response)` result in place of `model`. Selection
then depends on those responses. The covariance used to make each held-out
prediction should still be estimated from that fold's training data only.

## Add kNNDM when appropriate

kNNDM is a candidate CV construction, whereas `W` and `J2` are criteria that can
evaluate it alongside the other candidates. The optional constructor uses the
implementation in **CAST**. It currently constructs folds for equally weighted
target points. For a weighted target you may audit externally supplied folds, but
the CAST construction itself does not optimise those weights.

```{r knndm, eval=FALSE}
install.packages(c("sf", "CAST"))
equal_target <- prediction_target(q)
schemes$knndm <- spatial_folds(training, 5, "knndm",
                              target = equal_target, seed = 4)
compare_cv_schemes(training, schemes, equal_target, model, criterion = "J2")
```

## Evaluate a rule when the generating distribution is known

In a simulation, `gaussian_cv()` can calculate expected CV MSE and target MSE
without simulating responses. This example assumes the known-mean Gaussian model
with the covariance specified above. All schemes share the same target MSE.

```{r reference}
reference <- lapply(schemes, function(f) gaussian_cv(training, f, target, model))
evaluation <- data.frame(
  scheme = names(schemes),
  target_mse = vapply(reference, `[[`, numeric(1), "target_mse"),
  cv_mse = vapply(reference, `[[`, numeric(1), "cv_mse"),
  absolute_bias = abs(vapply(reference, `[[`, numeric(1), "optimism"))
)
evaluation
```

The best scheme by `absolute_bias` is the one whose **expected CV MSE is closest
to target MSE**. Target MSE is used here only for evaluation, after the diagnostic
choices were made. In an application it is not usually known.

## Handle ties without using target errors

```{r ties}
same <- list(first = schemes$random, second = schemes$random)
tied <- compare_cv_schemes(training, same, target, model)
tied$table[, c("scheme", "criterion_value", "selection_probability")]
```

If two schemes tie, a rule that chooses uniformly between them has expected
evaluation loss equal to the average of their **individual losses**. For example,
signed estimation errors $-0.1$ and $0.1$ give average absolute error 0.1. Averaging
the signed errors first would give zero and would assess a different estimator.

```{r evaluation-loss}
sum(by_J2$table$selection_probability * evaluation$absolute_bias)
```

The default absolute tie tolerance is $10^{-12}$ in criterion units. Report and
check that tolerance when very weak correlation makes all contrasts tiny.
With zero spatial signal, all `J2` values are zero and all candidates tie.
